'''Sabine Kraml''' (born 19 July 1971 in [[Steyr]]) is an Austrian physicist, specializing in theoretical [[high energy physics]].

== Education and career ==
In 1994, Kraml received the degree of Diplomingenieur (equivalent to a master's degree) and in 1999 her Ph.D., both from the [[TU Wien]]. The Ph.D.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last=Kraml |first=Sabine |date=1999-03-04 |title=Stop and Sbottom Phenomenology in the MSSM, Ph.D. thesis (1999) |eprint=hep-ph/9903257 }}</ref> was carried out at the Institute of High Energy Physics (HEPHY) of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] with Dr. Walter Majerotto as [[doctoral advisor]]. After a further year at the HEPHY, she worked from 2001 to 2007 as a postdoc at [[CERN]]. In 2007, she obtained her habilitation from the [[University of Innsbruck]]. In the same year, she was hired at the French [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] and moved to the LPSC in Grenoble, France, where she is still today.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Melchor |first=Stephanie |date=2021-01-14 |title=ATLAS releases 'full orchestra' of analysis instruments {{!}} symmetry magazine |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/atlas-releases-full-orchestra-of-analysis-instruments?language_content_entity=und |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=www.symmetrymagazine.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=cern |date=2021-04-28 |title=LHC reinterpreters think long-term |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/lhc-reinterpreters-think-long-term/ |access-date=2025-04-22 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-US}}</ref>

Her research deals with physics beyond the [[Standard Model]], in particular the phenomenology of weak-scale [[supersymmetry]] at colliders, non-standard [[Higgs boson|Higgs]] physics and particle [[dark matter]]. Most of her publications relate directly to experiment, from computing the effects of new physics, to interpreting measurements and the results of searches for new particles. In 2008 she was elected `young member' of the [[Austrian Academy of Sciences]] (appointment for 10 years).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ehemalige Mitglieder Junge Akademie |url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/junge-akademie/1/ehemalige-mitglieder-junge-akademie |access-date=2024-01-21 |website=www.oeaw.ac.at}}</ref> In 2012 she was promoted to the rank of research director of the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] 2nd class (DR2) and in 2018 to 1st class (DR1). In 2024, she was proposed for promotion to `Exceptional class' (DRCE1) by both CNRS sections 01<ref>{{cite web |title=CoNRS Section 01: Session Automne 2024 |url=https://section01.in2p3.fr/2024/10/04/session-automne-2024/}}</ref> and 02.<ref>{{cite web |title=CoNRS Section 02: Session Automne 2024 |url=http://www.lpthe.jussieu.fr/section02/session_docs/PV_A24_section02.pdf}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
In private life, she is a mountaineer and martial arts practitioner.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-10-18 |title=Article du Dauphiné Libéré du 12/10/22 – École Shin-do |url=https://shindokarate.fr/2022/10/18/article-du-dauphine-libere-du-12-10-22/ |access-date=2024-01-30 |language=fr-FR}}</ref>
